data.title: Sierra, led by former Salesforce co-CEO, may raise funds at $30B valuation: report
data.description:
• Artificial intelligence startup Sierra, led by former Salesforce (CRM) co-CEO Bret Taylor, is in talks with investors to raise funds at a $30B valuation, The Information reported.
  • The startup could raise around $1.5B in new funding, which would double the $15B valuation it achieved in May, the news outlet added, citing two people with knowledge of the fundraising. The talks are still ongoing, and terms of the deal could change.
  • Sierra did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.
  • Based in San Francisco, Sierra said in October that it had surpassed $400M in annualized revenue. Sierra creates AI agents for customer experience teams and developers via its Agent OS.
  • Sierra raised $350M in funding in September 2025, giving the company a $10B valuation.

data.title: Kalshi asks states for help in restricting problem gamblers - report
data.description:
Kalshi (KALSHI) is seeking to enlist states' assistance to deal with problem gamblers who want to place bets on the prediction markets venue, according to a media report on Thursday.

The company, in partnership with smaller rival Novig, sent a letter to 35 states, asking them to share so-called "self-exclusion lists" that identify gambling addicts who want to be restricted from access to betting websites, Bloomberg News reported, citing the letter it reviewed.

"We believe a person’s choice to self-exclude should not depend on where they live or which regulator oversees a platform," Kalshi and Novig said in the letter, as reported by Bloomberg. "Today’s patchwork of separate state lists leaves gaps that at-risk people can fall through."

The appeal to states comes as Kalshi is fighting numerous lawsuits, which allege that the company is running afoul of state gambling laws. The states involved contend that prediction markets should be overseen by state gaming regulators.

Kalshi (KALSHI), however, says it's a financial exchange, not a gambling business, and is subject to federal regulators, specifically the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

The prediction market operator keeps a self-exclusion list with IC360, a compliance firm for the gambling industry. That list includes about 1,800 who have signed up to be excluded from prediction markets, Bloomberg said. Kalshi and Novig offered to share those names with the states to be combined with the tens of thousands of bettors in the state-run databases.

The company asked that states respond by Dec. 15. "A single federal self-exclusion program can protect every person who asks for it, on every platform, in every state," the letter said, according to the report.

data.title: Evonik plunges after BASF drops takeover over
data.description:
Evonik (EVKIF) (EVKIY) sank 17% in German trading after BASF (BASFY) (BFFAF) dropped its efforts to purchase the chemicals company.  BASF rose as much as 2.9%.

The decision follows Evonik’s rejection of two non-binding all-cash offers made by BASF (BASFY).

"Despite the indication that BASF was prepared to consider a further moderate increase to its offer, the Executive Board of Evonik has not shown meaningful engagement until today," BASF said in a statement on Thursday. "At the same time, BASF’s assessment of Evonik’s standalone prospects and associated risks did not provide sufficient grounds to justify a higher valuation. Against this background, BASF does not consider it to be in the best interests of its shareholders to pursue the transaction at a higher price."

Evonik (EVKIY) late last month said it won't enter into negotiations with BASF (BASFY) (BFFAF), which made an increased €11.2B (~$12.5B) offer for Germany’s second-largest chemical maker.

BASF has argued that a combination would strengthen the two companies against competitors from China and elsewhere; while Evonik (EVKIF) (EVKIY) is BASF's preferred acquisition target, the company is weighing other opportunities, CEO Markus Kamieth said on the company's earnings conference call.

data.title: U.S. equities trade mixed ahead of Anthropic debut
data.description:
Wall Street’s major market averages are mixed on Thursday, with technology shares leading the gains, as investors turned their attention to the highly anticipated public debut of artificial intelligence startup Anthropic (ANT).

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was near even, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +0.5%.

From a sector-by-sector basis, two of the 11 segments were in positive trading territory, with communication services leading the charge and consumer staples struggling the most. 

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after pricing its IPO at $83 a share, above its expected range. The company raised approximately $81.3 billion, and its debut could offer a gauge of how public-market investors are assessing the longer-term commercial prospects of AI amid recent weakness in several AI-linked stocks. 

Meanwhile, for the week ended Nov. 14, initial jobless claims in the U.S. rose by 1K to 203K, edging past the 198K consensus, according to data released by the U.S. Department of Labor. 

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) added 1 basis point to 4.81%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked up 1 basis point to 5.07%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) inched up 1 basis point to 5.42%. 

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of PDD Holdings (PDD) advanced +10.5%, while shares of Williams-Sonoma (WSM) dropped -7.9%.

data.title: All In FutureTech Alliance to acquire California's Little Vault for $8M
data.description:
• All In FutureTech Alliance (AIFA) announced on Thursday that it will acquire all shares of Little Vault, a corporation incorporated in California, for $8M.
  • Under the agreement, AIFA will issue 1,280,000 shares of its common stock to Shanglong Li, the seller, at an agreed reference price of $6.25 per share.
  • The acquisition is intended to advance the implementation of the company’s business strategy in content IP commercialization, digital content services, and the creator economy, while facilitating the phased development and commercialization of its AI-powered application products, AIFA said.
  • The transaction will be paid entirely in shares, and the company will not pay cash consideration to the seller for the acquisition.
  • Press Release

data.title: Trident secures $15M private placement to fund expansion into energy infrastructure for data centres
data.description:
Trident Digital Tech (TDTH) announced Thursday that it has entered into a subscription agreement with Robinhood Ventures for a private placement of 10M class B ordinary shares of the company at $1.50 per share, for an aggregate purchase price of $15M. 

Shares of TDTH slipped nearly 55% at $0.33 during early trading hours. 

The Company intends to use the proceeds of the Private Placement to partially fund its contemplated acquisition of the controlling stake in Guang Yao Development (M) Sdn. Bhd. (“Guang Yao”), a Malaysian company positioned to develop and provide hydrogen power and battery energy storage solutions for data centres and partially for its general corporate purposes. 

The closing of the private placement is not conditional on the completion of that acquisition transaction, the firm highlighted, adding that "if the proposed acquisition transaction is not completed, the company intends to use all the net proceeds of the private placement for working capital and general corporate purposes."

Source: press release

data.title: S&P 500 typical pattern shows a rally after the holiday’s rollercoaster
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) has historically gained around 2.4% from mid-November through year-end, according to Goldman Sachs analysts, who note that positive seasonality during the November-December period is now well-known among investors.

Goldman Sachs identifies a clear four-phase “holiday” pattern in market performance: a mid-November dip, a Thanksgiving ramp-up, an early December stall, and then a late December rally.

 

 

 

The analysts note that performance has historically received a boost in the immediate Thanksgiving period, stalled out in early December, only to be reignited once again in the next round of holiday cheer.

The late-December rally has proven particularly reliable, according to Goldman Sachs data. From December 15 to year-end, the S&P 500 (SP500) rose in 27 of 36 years since 1990, averaging a gain of 1.22%.

Goldman Sachs offers an important caveat, however, for years when volatility starts elevated.

In the 17 years since 1990, when the VIX (VIX) started mid-November at 18 or higher—it's currently around 22.82—the S&P 500's (SP500) year-end gain was smaller, averaging just 1.34% and rising in only 59% of years, with a median drawdown of 3%.

Despite the smaller gains in high-volatility years, Goldman Sachs notes that the VIX (VIX) itself typically calms down, falling by year-end in 14 of those 17 elevated-volatility years.

data.title: Apple ordered by UK government to maintain access to encrypted customer data
data.description:
Apple (AAPL) was ordered by the British government to maintain access to encrypted customer data so it could be made available to intelligence agencies, according to a ruling by a British tribunal.

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal said Apple was given a Technical Capability Notice requiring it to be able to access users' data in decrypted form.

The government had declined to comment on the existence of the notice, citing its policy of "neither confirm nor deny" on national security matters.

But the tribunal said senior British government officials had briefed several media outlets, including The Times and the Financial Times, about the order. "We infer that it is extremely unlikely that multiple Government sources would have briefed the media in the absence of authorisation for such briefing," said the Investigatory Powers Tribunal.

Apple is challenging the government's authority to issue the notice. The ruling allows much of Apple's legal challenge against the government to be heard in public, although details of the notice may remain confidential on national security grounds.

data.title: Arthur J. Gallagher acquires AgriServ
data.description:
Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. (AJG) on Thursday announced the acquisition of Panora, Iowa-based AgriServ, a specialist crop insurance broker serving farmers and agribusinesses throughout Iowa.

Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

As a part of the agreement, Jerod George, Cory Meinecke, Lucas Wendl, and the AgriServ team will join Gallagher (AJG)'s US crop and agricultural brokerage operations and report to Bumpy Triche, head of Gallagher's Southeast retail property/casualty brokerage operations.

Shares of AJG slipped nearly 2% during early trading hours. 

"AgriServ has a strong reputation in the agricultural niche and will further expand our crop insurance brokerage capabilities," said J. Patrick Gallagher, Jr., Chairman and CEO. "I am very pleased to welcome Jerod, Cory, Lucas, and their associates to Gallagher."

Source: press release
